chapter: Imperial Orchestra and Southern Rhythm Boys
title: Learning to arrange from Al Wilson in the Southern Rhythm Boys
summary: With the Southern Rhythm Boys she studied arranging under saxophonist Al Wilson and arranged for the 15 or 16 piece band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But at that time I was into the arranging thing, I was learning to arrange music. Yes, I wanted to study. I wanted to study arranging, and we had a very wonderful saxophone player and arranger in the band by the name of Al Wilson. Al was from New Orleans, and he taught me. I studied under him, he taught me how to arrange. So I was arranging for all of this band, and at that time we had about 15 pieces, I think, or 16 pieces.
Oh, this was the Southern Rhythm Boys.
It was called the Southern Rhythm Boys.
And in one of these groups I think Paul Barnes, the wonderful
Paul Barnes, from New Orleans, was in this group. Also at one time, Collins, Neil Collins -- not Neil Collins.
